::: {.page-band}

## Data Systems

::: {.method-panel-grid}
::: {.method-panel}
### Longitudinal Relational Data

Career histories, institutions, cities, publications, collaboration ties, mobility events, and city attributes are linked into temporally ordered data systems for scientific-career research.
:::

::: {.method-panel}
### Bibliometric and Institutional Linkage

Scopus, OpenAlex, ROR, affiliation strings, institution names, and geocoded city fields are handled through source-aware linkage and conflict auditing.
:::

::: {.method-panel}
### Spatial and Innovation Data

Supporting materials include VIIRS-DNB nighttime lights, UN Comtrade, patent and trademark records, R&D firm-year data, city indicators, and policy or planning documents where sharing permissions allow.
:::
:::

:::

::: {.page-band .surface}

## Data Construction and Measurement

::: {.method-chain}
::: {.method-row}
### Career, Institution, and City Reconstruction

Person validation, institution normalisation, city standardisation, temporal auditing, and education-employment separation make career histories comparable over time.
:::

::: {.method-row}
### Relational Measurement

Coauthorship, mobility ties, publication-location fields, historical platform ties, ego-network measures, and candidate destinations are measured as distinct constructs rather than interchangeable proxies.
:::

::: {.method-row}
### Innovation Measurement

Firm-year innovation work links R&D, patents, trademarks, industry, country, identity, and year to compare technological and market-facing innovation without reducing innovation to one count.
:::

::: {.method-row}
### Spatial and Temporal Indicators

Remote-sensing and trade-network projects use spatial aggregation, Fisher Information, DTW, K-Means, directed weighted networks, and temporal comparison.
:::
:::

:::

::: {.page-band}

## Empirical Design and Modelling

::: {.method-chain}
::: {.method-row}
### Choice Modelling

Observed moves are organised as event-specific choice sets, with selected destinations compared against alternatives and predictors measured before the move.
:::

::: {.method-row}
### Network Analysis

Directed weighted mobility networks, centrality, core structure, ego networks, WERGM, proximity measures, and tie persistence are used to connect macro structures with individual career trajectories.
:::

::: {.method-row}
### Comparative and Econometric Designs

The current empirical toolkit includes conditional logit, clustered robust inference, Heckman two-stage models, OLS, robustness checks, sensitivity analysis, and longitudinal comparison.
:::

::: {.method-row}
### Method Boundaries

The public profile does not claim deep learning, causal discovery, causal representation learning, survey experimentation, or autonomous LLM research as completed expertise.
:::
:::

:::

::: {.page-band .surface}

## Reproducibility and Research Software

::: {.method-chain}
::: {.method-row}
### Workflow

Research workflows emphasise scripted processing, version control, synthetic fixtures, data-quality audits, source-conflict logs, and separation between public descriptions and restricted data.
:::

::: {.method-row}
### Software Environment

Python, R, Stata, ArcGIS/QGIS, NetworkX, Gephi, UCINET, Scimago Graphica, Git, GitHub, and Quarto are used for data construction, modelling, documentation, and publication workflows.
:::

::: {.method-row}
### Scopus Research Data Toolkit

The public toolkit supports author-institution-city linkage with synthetic fixtures, offline mock transport, tests, and documentation. It does not bundle licensed Scopus records.

[GitHub](https://github.com/Olivia-wr-research/author-institution-city-linkage){.btn .btn-secondary}
:::
:::
